cases.situation: Leo has no safety-net record at all, so the default applies: protection on, the starter size, nothing saved. He has $800 spare this month and is looking at a $500 purchase. It is bought on 15 November 2026 (today), paid in one go. A usual month: pay $3,000, bills $1,400 and everyday spending $800 ($500 of it on essentials).
cases.why: No record means the default: protection on, a starter size of one month of essential costs ($1,400 bills + $500 essential everyday spending = $1,900), and $0 saved. Only money already in the net is protected, so nothing is held back (D-35): $800 spare - $500 = $300 left. $300 is not under the tight floor of $220 (a tenth of $1,400 bills + $800 everyday spending), so the answer is the amber "Fits, but no safety net", with "Nothing is saved for emergencies yet. One month of essential costs is about $1,900. 1 month is a start; 3 to 6 months is common." It never says a safety net is "untouched" (D-25).

cases.situation: Noor is paid $1,400 every two weeks: on 13 November and next on 27 November. On 15 November she has $1,400 in her account and a full $1,700 safety net. Rent of $600 is due on 20 November. Counting the pay on the 27th, November leaves $800 spare. She is looking at a $700 purchase. It is bought on 15 November 2026 (today), paid in one go. A usual month: pay $1,400 every two weeks, bills $1,200 and everyday spending $800 ($500 of it on essentials).
cases.why: Spare money says yes ($800 - $700 = $100), but the day-by-day path does not. The $400 of everyday spending still to come is spread evenly, $25 a day over the 16 days from 15 to 30 November. After rent on the 20th the account goes below $0, reaching $1,400 - $600 rent - $300 everyday spending (15 to 26 November) - $700 = -$200 on 26 November. So the answer says it "needs $200 from your safety net until 27 Nov", the next payday. The path must stay above the net (FIN-02), so this is "Dips into your safety net", not a plain "Fits". It adds "Waiting until 27 Nov keeps your safety net whole."

cases.persona: Maya, freelancer, no pay series (invented, D-52)
cases.situation: Maya is a freelancer with no scheduled pay. Over the last six months (April to September) she was paid $3,100, $2,900, $3,000, $3,200, $2,800 and $3,000, always on the 5th; her lowest month was $2,800. $3,000 came in on 1 October. By 3 October she has paid rent $1,000, phone $200 and her $200 monthly transfer to savings (bills $1,400 in all) and spent $50; $2,050 is in her everyday account and $3,000 sits in her savings account marked as her safety net (locked, the default). She is looking at a $60 purchase. It is bought on 3 October 2026 (today), paid in one go. A usual month: pay $3,000 (her own steady figure), bills $1,400 and everyday spending $800 (all of it on essentials).
cases.why: D-52: with no pay series but six full months of history, pay is expected on her usual payday (the 5th) at her lowest month ($2,800), so November and December each bring $2,800 on the 5th. October: $3,000 in - $1,400 bills - $50 spent - $750 everyday still to come = $800 left; $800 - $60 = $740, a plain "Fits" from this month's money. $740 is over the tight floor of $220 (a tenth of $1,400 bills + $800 everyday spending). The safety net's starter size is $2,200 ($1,400 bills + $800 essential spending), so $800 of her $3,000 is extra savings. Her everyday account alone would reach about $266.67 below $0 on 4 November ($2,050 - $60 - $750 in October, then $1,400 of bills on 1 November and about $26.67 a day of everyday spending until her pay on the 5th); with the $800 of extra savings the path stays at about $533 above $0, so the net is not needed and the answer adds, as a timing fact (D-58), "Move $266.67 from your savings to your everyday account by 1 November."
cases.plannerNote: From the plan-18 audit (Maya $60). The audit has the $200 saving due on 6 October and the bills on 1-2 November with a low of about +$1,133 on 4 November; this fixture has no saving line, so the saving is stated as a bill already paid (bills $1,400, everyday account $2,050), which gives the same $740.
